licence: unclear (README names LGPL-3.0; LICENSE.GPL is GPL-3.0; LICENSE.MIT is MIT)

data_fields.name: stack_amount_check
data_fields.donor_constant: rule: item.Count >= requested amount (count not used to split the stack)

data_fields.name: settle_money_check
data_fields.donor_constant: rule: offered money <= cash on hand, checked at settle

data_fields.name: free_slot_check
data_fields.donor_constant: rule: free bag slots >= incoming item count (slots, not stack space)

data_fields.name: ok_requires_locks
data_fields.donor_constant: rule: donor accepts ok if either side locked (comment says both); sketch requires both

best_idea: Lock first, then ok; any change or unlock clears both oks, and only a both-locked, both-ok pair triggers one atomic settle.
decision_why: Lock-on-change with both-ok is the anti-scam shape we need; the donor's stale ok flags, partial settle, whole-stack move and missing bind check are defects fixed in origins/server/trade.ts, and the licence is unclear so it is clean-room only.
acceptance: A offers one stack of 20 and 500 coins; both lock; B oks; A changes coins to 5 and both locks and oks clear on both screens; both lock and ok again; one settle() writes one item row with count 20 and one money row under one trade id; a server test asserts that an ok given before a change settles nothing and that a bind-on-pickup item is refused at add.
